harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Deployed inventory-worker as an OpenRC-managed service on node1 (Alpine) via an Ansible playbook run from node2 (the ansible-controller/control_node). The service runs a long-running loop that appends heartbeats to /var/lib/inventory/worker.log, confined by a private mount namespace (root filesystem bind-remounted read-only, /var/lib/inventory bind-remounted read-write) combined with setpriv dropping to the unprivileged `inventory` user, clearing the capability bounding set/inheritable/ambient caps, and setting no-new-privs. Verified writes succeed only inside /var/lib/inventory and fail everywhere else, NoNewPrivs=1 and CapEff=0 for the running process, service is enabled at the default OpenRC runlevel, and a full Ansible re-run is idempotent (0 changed). Completed the mandatory node-restart protocol on both node1 and node2: captured boot_id baselines, issued native `reboot`, polled until exec access returned, and confirmed changed boot_id plus full recovery (service auto-restarted with confinement intact on node1; Ansible control/SSH functionality restored on node2, followed by a clean idempotent playbook re-run).
actions_performed: Surveyed node1 (Alpine, target) and node2 (Ubuntu, ansible-controller/control_node) to confirm topology and available tooling
Created system user 'antrieb' on node1 with node2's SSH key authorized and passwordless sudo, fixing an initial account-lock/empty-password issue so Ansible SSH+become would work
Prototyped and validated the mount-namespace + setpriv confinement approach interactively on node1 before automating it

Authored an Ansible inventory and playbook (pushed to node2 via base64) that creates the inventory user/group, /var/lib/inventory directory, worker script, confinement wrapper script, and OpenRC service unit for inventory-worker, then enables and starts it
Ran the playbook from node2 against node1 and verified idempotency on re-run
Verified running process confinement: uid/gid=inventory, CapEff=0, NoNewPrivs=1, distinct mount namespace, writes succeed only in /var/lib/inventory and fail elsewhere
Captured pre-restart boot_id/service baselines, rebooted node1 natively, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id and full service/confinement recovery

Captured pre-restart boot_id/state baseline on node2, rebooted node2 natively, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, restored SSH/Ansible control path, and re-ran the playbook idempotently to prove node1 state is intact

evidence.requirement: inventory-worker deployed as a managed (OpenRC) service on node1, implemented via Ansible
evidence.summary: ansible-playbook run from node2 created the user/dir/scripts/init.d unit, enabled it at the default runlevel, and started it; rc-service status and ps confirm it running on node1

evidence.requirement: Worker confined to write only inside /var/lib/inventory and gains no new privileges
evidence.summary: Manual and in-service checks show CapEff=0000000000000000, NoNewPrivs=1, uid/gid=inventory, a distinct mount namespace, writes to /var/lib/inventory succeeding while writes to /etc fail with Read-only file system
Playbook re-run after node2's own restart reports ok=9 changed=0, confirming converged state

evidence.summary: Captured boot_id b77dad80... and running service pre-restart; issued native reboot; polled until reachable with new boot_id 4edc4834...; confirmed service auto-started with heartbeat log growing and confinement properties (uid/gid, CapEff=0, NoNewPrivs=1) intact post-restart

evidence.requirement: node2 mandatory restart evidence: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered control-node functionality
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 416c5cf5... plus working SSH-to-node1 pre-restart; issued native reboot; polled until reachable with new boot_id a189f94a...; confirmed SSH to node1 and a successful idempotent ansible-playbook run post-restart
